mainTopic: The כהנים' garments at night, benefit from בגדי כהונה, and lessons from the משנה on modesty, health and respect
overview: The amud opens with a problem. The משנה says the כהנים slept with their garments under their heads, but the אבנט may contain כלאים, and חכמים forbade lying on כלאים even with ten mattresses in between. The גמרא gives three answers: the garments were placed next to their heads, or only the garments without כלאים went under them, or (רב אשי) בגדי כהונה are stiff and stiff כלאים is permitted. A ברייתא then proves that benefit from בגדי כהונה inside the מקדש is allowed, though wearing them outside is forbidden. The story of שמעון הצדיק on the day of הר גריזים is explained in two ways: either the garments were only fit to be בגדי כהונה, or it was an emergency of עת לעשות לה׳. The impure כהן leaving through the tunnels supports רבי יוחנן, who says the tunnels were never made holy. The משנה's honorable בית הכסא leads to a story about רב ספרא and רבי אבא. It also leads to advice from רב and רב הונא to their sons on health, modesty, and respect for a teacher. The amud ends by quoting a משנה about the איש הר הבית checking the guards at night, which continues on the next amud.

steps.title: The problem of the belt made of wool and linen
steps.stepSummary: Putting the garments under the head works only if the ordinary כהן's אבנט has no כלאים. But according to the view that it is the same as the כהן גדול's אבנט, which has כלאים, how could they lie on it?
steps.simpleTranslation: This works well for the one who says the כהן גדול's belt is different from the ordinary כהן's belt. But for the one who says they are the same belt, what can we say?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the משנה's statement that the כהנים put their garments under their heads. One of those garments, the belt, may contain כלאים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The כהן גדול's אבנט was made of wool and linen. If the ordinary כהן's אבנט was plain linen, there is no problem. But according to the opinion that the ordinary כהן's belt is identical, the כהנים would be lying on כלאים, so the משנה needs an explanation.

keyTerms.meaning: The belt worn by the כהנים
It works out well (for this opinion)
What is there to say? (a challenge to the other opinion)

steps.confusionAlert: The גמרא is not saying the כהנים did something wrong. It is asking how the משנה can be read so that it fits the opinion that the ordinary כהן's belt had כלאים.

phrases.english: It works out well according to the one who said
the belt of the High Priest
phrases.notes: The High Priest's belt was woven from wool and linen together, which is כלאים.

phrases.aramaic: לֹא זֶהוּ אַבְנֵטוֹ שֶׁל כֹּהֵן הֶדְיוֹט.
phrases.english: is not the same as the belt of an ordinary priest.
But according to the one who said
the belt of an ordinary priest
is the same as the belt of the High Priest,
what is there to say?
phrases.notes: In other words: how can the כהנים lie on a belt that has כלאים in it?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens the difficulty about the משנה's phrase 'under their heads'
steps.kashyaTarget: The משנה's statement that the כהנים placed their garments under their heads
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If the ordinary כהן's אבנט contains כלאים, lying on it should be forbidden

steps.title: Suggestion: only wearing כלאים is forbidden, not lying on it
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא proposes that the איסור of כלאים covers only putting on and wearing the garment. Spreading it underneath oneself would be fine.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if you say that with כלאים only putting it on and wearing it is forbidden, but spreading it under yourself is fine…
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא suggests a possible way out of the problem. This sets up the next step, where the suggestion is knocked down.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If lying on כלאים were allowed, the משנה would have no problem even with a belt that contains כלאים. This is a 'what if you say' answer, a proposal the גמרא is about to test.

keyTerms.meaning: Forbidden mixture, here wool and linen woven together (שעטנז)
And if you would say (introduces a proposed answer)

phrases.english: And if you would say:
with diverse kinds, it is only putting on and wearing that is forbidden,
but spreading it beneath oneself is fine,

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Proposes an answer to the קשיא of step 1
steps.terutzResolutionType: Narrowing the scope of the איסור
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Lying on a כלאים belt is forbidden
steps.terutzMaskana: The איסור of כלאים covers only wearing, so lying on it is permitted

steps.title: A ברייתא forbids lying on כלאים מדרבנן
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא says that by תורה law you may spread כלאים under you, but חכמים forbade it in case a thread wraps around your body.
steps.simpleTranslation: But a ברייתא teaches: 'It shall not come upon you', but you may spread it under you. However, חכמים said it is forbidden, in case one thread wraps onto his skin.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא rejects the suggestion of step 2. Even though the תורה allows lying on כלאים, the rabbis forbade it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא agrees that the פסוק itself only forbids having כלאים 'on' you. But חכמים made a גזירה against lying on it, because a loose thread could wrap around the body and turn it into wearing. So the כהנים still could not lie on a כלאים belt.

keyTerms.meaning: 'It shall not come upon you' (ויקרא 19:19), the source of the כלאים clothing איסור

phrases.english: But isn't it taught in a baraita:
"Shall not come upon you"
but you may spread it beneath you.
But the Sages said:
it is forbidden to do so,

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁמָּא תִּיכָּרֵךְ נִימָא אַחַת עַל בְּשָׂרוֹ.
phrases.english: lest a single fiber wrap itself onto his flesh.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the answer of step 2
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Fully rejects the idea that lying on כלאים is permitted in practice
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: It ignores the rabbinic גזירה against spreading כלאים under oneself

steps.title: Suggestion: something separates the כהן from the garment
steps.stepSummary: Maybe the כהנים put something between themselves and the garments, so no thread could wrap onto their skin.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if you say that something separated between them…
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tries a second way out: put a barrier in between, so the rabbis' worry does not apply. This sets up the next rejection.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The rabbis' reason in step 3 was the fear of a thread wrapping onto the skin. If something separates the כהן from the garment, that fear seems to disappear, so maybe it is allowed.

phrases.english: And if you would say that something separates,

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a new answer that tries to get around the reason in step 3
steps.terutzResolutionType: Removing the reason behind the גזירה
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The rabbinic איסור applies to the כהנים
steps.terutzMaskana: With a barrier, the worry about threads is gone, so it would be permitted

steps.title: Even ten mattresses do not help
steps.stepSummary: A tradition from the holy community in ירושלים says that even with ten mattresses on top of כלאים, sleeping on them is forbidden.
steps.simpleTranslation: But didn't רבי שמעון say in the name of רבי יהושע בן לוי, in the name of רבי יוסי בן שאול, in the name of the holy community in ירושלים: even ten mattresses one on top of the other, with כלאים beneath them, it is forbidden to sleep on them?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא rejects the barrier idea of step 4. Separation does not help at all.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Ten mattresses is clearly enough to keep any thread away from the skin, and still it is forbidden. This shows that the rabbis' rule applies across the board, even when the worry behind it is missing. So a barrier cannot save the כהנים.

keyTerms.meaning: The holy community (a group of sages in ירושלים)
One on top of the other

phrases.english: But didn't Rabbi Shimon say,
that Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi said,
that Rabbi Yosei ben Shaul said
in the name of the holy community in Jerusalem:

phrases.aramaic: אֲפִילּוּ עֶשֶׂר מַצָּעוֹת זוֹ עַל גַּב זוֹ,
phrases.english: Even ten mattresses one on top of the other,
with diverse kinds beneath them,
it is forbidden to sleep on them.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the barrier answer of step 4
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Fully rejects the idea that a barrier permits lying on כלאים
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The rabbinic איסור applies even when the thread worry is removed

steps.title: So the garments were placed next to their heads
steps.stepSummary: Since both defenses failed, the גמרא concludes that the משנה means the garments were placed next to the כהנים' heads, not under them.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, learn from this: next to their heads.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא draws its conclusion. The משנה's 'under their heads' really means 'next to their heads'.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Lying on the belt cannot be permitted, and a barrier does not help. So the only way to keep the משנה consistent with the opinion that the ordinary כהן's belt has כלאים is to read it as 'beside their heads'.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather (introduces the conclusion after rejecting other options)
Learn from this, conclude from here

steps.whatToRemember: First answer: the משנה's 'under their heads' means 'next to their heads', because lying on כלאים is forbidden מדרבנן even with ten mattresses in between.

phrases.english: Rather, conclude from this:
next to their heads.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Concludes after both defenses were rejected
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The garments were placed beside the כהנים' heads, not under them

steps.title: Only the garments without כלאים went under their heads
steps.stepSummary: Another answer: the משנה really means under their heads, but only the garments that have no כלאים.
steps.simpleTranslation: Or, if you like, say: it is talking about the garments that have no כלאים.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא offers a different answer that keeps 'under their heads' as written. It limits the משנה to the garments without כלאים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Only the אבנט had כלאים. The other garments were pure linen, so placing those under the head is no problem. The belt would simply be kept somewhere else.

keyTerms.meaning: And if you want, say (introduces an alternative answer)

phrases.english: And if you wish, say:
it refers to those garments that do not contain diverse kinds.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a different answer to the קשיא of step 1 instead of the conclusion in step 6
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limiting the case of the משנה
steps.terutzHavaAmina: All the garments, including the belt, went under their heads
steps.terutzMaskana: Only the garments without כלאים were placed under their heads

steps.title: רב אשי: בגדי כהונה are stiff
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי answers that even the belt may go under their heads, because בגדי כהונה are stiff fabric.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אשי said: בגדי כהונה are stiff.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי gives a third answer. Even the כלאים belt is allowed under their heads, because the material is stiff.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The איסור of כלאים applies to soft fabric that feels like clothing. Stiff fabric is not treated that way, so lying on it is not a problem. The next step brings a source for this idea.

phrases.english: Rav Ashi said:
the priestly garments are stiff,

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A further alternative answer to the קשיא of step 1
steps.terutzResolutionType: Exception based on the type of material
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Any fabric of כלאים is forbidden to lie on
steps.terutzMaskana: Stiff fabric is not included in the איסור, so even the belt may go under their heads

steps.title: Proof: the stiff felt of נרש is permitted
steps.stepSummary: רב הונא בריה דרב יהושע ruled that a stiff felt made in נרש is permitted even though it has כלאים, which supports רב אשי.
steps.simpleTranslation: As רב הונא son of רב יהושע said: this stiff felt of נרש is permitted.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא backs up רב אשי with a ruling that stiff כלאים material is permitted.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The felt made in the town of נרש was stiff, and רב הונא בריה דרב יהושע allowed it. This shows that stiffness takes fabric out of the כלאים איסור, so the stiff בגדי כהונה may be placed under the head.

keyTerms.meaning: A town in בבל where this felt was made

steps.whatToRemember: Three answers to the belt problem: (1) the garments were next to their heads; (2) only the garments without כלאים went under their heads; (3) רב אשי: בגדי כהונה are stiff, and stiff כלאים fabric is permitted, like the felt of נרש.

phrases.aramaic: דְּאָמַר רַב הוּנָא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב יְהוֹשֻׁעַ:
phrases.english: As Rav Huna son of Rav Yehoshua said:
This stiff felt of Neresh
is permitted.

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּאָמַר רַב הוּנָא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב יְהוֹשֻׁעַ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports רב אשי's answer in step 8
steps.raayaObject: רב אשי's claim that stiff garments are not forbidden as כלאים
steps.raayaSupportSource: רב הונא בריה דרב יהושע's ruling permitting the stiff felt of נרש

steps.title: A ברייתא proves the priestly garments may be enjoyed
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא says wearing בגדי כהונה outside the מקדש is forbidden, but inside the מקדש it is allowed even when not serving, because they were given to be enjoyed. This proves benefit from them is permitted.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear: בגדי כהונה: one who goes out in them to the outside world is forbidden. But in the מקדש, whether during service or not during service, it is permitted, because בגדי כהונה were given to be enjoyed. Learn from this.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to the question of whether the כהנים may get personal benefit from בגדי כהונה, and brings a ברייתא that answers it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא allows wearing the garments in the מקדש even when no service is being done. That only makes sense if using them for personal benefit is allowed, and the ברייתא says so outright: they were given to be enjoyed.

keyTerms.meaning: The special garments the כהנים wear for the service
Here: the outside world, anywhere outside the מקדש
The time the כהן is actually doing the service
They were given to be enjoyed (personal benefit is allowed)
Learn from this; the proof is accepted

steps.whyThisMatters: This settles the earlier question: getting personal benefit from בגדי כהונה is allowed, at least inside the מקדש.

phrases.english: Come and hear:
Priestly garments:
one who goes out in them to the outside world is forbidden.
phrases.notes: Literally "to the country." He means anywhere outside the מקדש.

phrases.english: But in the Temple, whether at the time of service
or not at the time of service, it is permitted,

phrases.aramaic: מִפְּנֵי שֶׁבִּגְדֵי כְהוּנָּה נִיתְּנוּ לֵיהָנוֹת בָּהֶן.
phrases.english: because priestly garments were given to be enjoyed.
Learn from this.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּא שְׁמַע: בִּגְדֵי כְהוּנָּה, הַיּוֹצֵא בָּהֶן לִמְדִינָה – אָסוּר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Goes back to the earlier question about benefit from בגדי כהונה and settles it with a ברייתא.
steps.raayaObject: That personal benefit from בגדי כהונה is permitted
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא allowing the garments to be worn in the מקדש even outside service time, because they were given to be enjoyed

steps.title: But the כהן גדול wore them outside on the day of הר גריזים
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the ברייתא's rule against wearing the garments outside. A ברייתא about the twenty-first of the month, the day of הר גריזים, describes the כהן גדול wearing them outside the מקדש.
steps.simpleTranslation: And outside the מקדש it is not allowed? But it was taught: On the twenty-first of the month is the day of הר גריזים, when one may not eulogize, as it says in מסכת יומא, in the chapter 'בא לו כהן גדול'.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the first half of the ברייתא, which forbids wearing בגדי כהונה outside the מקדש. It points to a famous story in מסכת יומא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: On the day of הר גריזים, a joyful day when eulogies are not allowed, the כהן גדול went out to meet the king while wearing בגדי כהונה. If going out in them is forbidden, how could he do that?

keyTerms.meaning: The day of הר גריזים, a joyful date when the מקדש was saved
To eulogize; not allowed on a joyful day
As it is found in another place

steps.confusionAlert: The question is not about benefit inside the מקדש, which was just proven. It is only about the ברייתא's rule that the garments may not be worn outside.

phrases.english: And outside the Temple it is not allowed?
But it was taught: On the twenty-first of it
phrases.notes: "Of it" means of the month of טבת.

phrases.english: is the day of Mount Gerizim, when one may not eulogize,
as it is found in Yoma, in the chapter
"The High Priest came close, etc."?!
phrases.notes: There, שמעון הצדיק goes out wearing בגדי כהונה to meet אלכסנדרוס מוקדון and saves the מקדש.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the first part of the ברייתא quoted in step 10.
steps.kashyaTarget: The ברייתא's rule that going out in בגדי כהונה is forbidden
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A ברייתא shows the כהן גדול wearing the garments outside the מקדש on the day of הר גריזים, which seems to contradict the ban.

steps.title: They were only garments fit to be priestly garments
steps.stepSummary: Following the passage in יומא, the first answer is that the כהן גדול was not wearing real holy בגדי כהונה, only garments that were fit to be used as them.
steps.simpleTranslation: Up to: If you want, say: they were garments fit to be בגדי כהונה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers using the explanation already given in מסכת יומא: the garments he wore outside were not really the holy ones.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ban only applies to holy בגדי כהונה. Garments that look the same and could become בגדי כהונה, but have not been made holy, may be worn anywhere. So there is no contradiction.

keyTerms.meaning: If you want, say; brings one possible answer
Fit or suitable for something, but not yet used for it

phrases.english: Up to: If you want, say:
phrases.notes: "Up to" means: read the passage in יומא until this point, where it gives its answers.

phrases.english: they were fit to be priestly garments.

steps.triggerLanguage: עַד אִיבָּעֵית אֵימָא: רְאוּיִין הֵן לְבִגְדֵי כְהוּנָּה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 11.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Redefining the case: the garments were not really holy בגדי כהונה
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The כהן גדול wore the actual holy garments outside the מקדש
steps.terutzMaskana: He wore garments only fit to be בגדי כהונה, so the ban did not apply

steps.title: An emergency to save the מקדש allows it
steps.stepSummary: A second answer: he did wear the real בגדי כהונה, but it was allowed because of the rule עת לעשות לה׳, which permits breaking a rule in an emergency for the sake of Heaven.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if you want, say: "It is time to act for ה׳; they have broken Your Torah."
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a second answer from יומא: even if they were the real holy garments, this was a special emergency.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This answer agrees that wearing real בגדי כהונה outside is normally forbidden. Saving the מקדש was such a great need that the rule of עת לעשות לה׳ allowed it. So the ברייתא's rule stands, and the story is a one-time exception.

keyTerms.meaning: A time to act for ה׳; in a real emergency for the sake of Heaven, a rule may be set aside

steps.whatToRemember: Benefit from בגדי כהונה inside the מקדש is allowed. Wearing them outside is forbidden. The הר גריזים story is explained either as garments only fit to be בגדי כהונה, or as an emergency under עת לעשות לה׳.
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that a clear rule can stay in force even when a famous story seems to break it, because the story may be a special emergency.

phrases.english: And if you want, say:
"It is time to act for the Lord; they have broken Your Torah."

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאִי בָּעֵית אֵימָא: עֵת לַעֲשׂוֹת לַה׳ הֵפֵרוּ תּוֹרָתֶךָ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second, different answer to the challenge of step 11.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Emergency exception: the rule applies, but was set aside
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The story shows that wearing the garments outside is simply allowed
steps.terutzMaskana: It is normally forbidden, but saving the מקדש made it allowed under עת לעשות לה׳

steps.title: The impure כהן's route supports רבי יוחנן on the tunnels
steps.stepSummary: The משנה says a כהן who had קרי walked out through the tunnels under the מקדש. This supports רבי יוחנן, who says the tunnels were never made holy.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said: if one of the כהנים had a seminal emission, and so on. This supports רבי יוחנן, who said: the tunnels were not made holy.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes a line from the משנה and shows that it backs up a ruling of רבי יוחנן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: An impure כהן is not allowed in holy areas, yet the משנה sends him out through the tunnels under the מקדש. That only works if the tunnels are not holy, which is exactly what רבי יוחנן says.

keyTerms.meaning: A seminal emission, which makes a person ritually impure

phrases.english: If a seminal emission befell one of them, etc.
This supports Rabbi Yochanan,
who said: The tunnels were not sanctified.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic on a different line of the משנה, after the discussion of wearing בגדי כהונה ends.
steps.raayaObject: רבי יוחנן's ruling that the tunnels under the מקדש were not sanctified.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה sends an impure כהן out through the tunnels, which would be forbidden if they were holy.

steps.title: A בעל קרי must leave two camps
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings another rule of רבי יוחנן: a בעל קרי is sent out of two camps.
steps.simpleTranslation: A person who had a seminal emission is sent outside of two camps.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא adds a related ruling of רבי יוחנן about how far a בעל קרי must stay away.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The two camps are the camp of the שכינה, which is the עזרה, and the camp of the לויים, which is the הר הבית. So the impure כהן may not stay in either of them. That is why he had to go out through the tunnels, which are not holy.

keyTerms.meaning: A person who had a seminal emission
Two camps: the camp of the שכינה (the עזרה) and the camp of the לויים (the הר הבית)

phrases.aramaic: בַּעַל קֶרִי מִשְׁתַּלֵּחַ חוּץ לִשְׁנֵי מַחֲנוֹת.
phrases.english: A man who experienced a seminal emission is sent outside of two camps.
phrases.notes: The two camps are the עזרה and the הר הבית.

steps.triggerLanguage: בַּעַל קֶרִי מִשְׁתַּלֵּחַ חוּץ לִשְׁנֵי מַחֲנוֹת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds another ruling of רבי יוחנן that fits the משנה's case of the impure כהן.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A בעל קרי must leave both the עזרה and the הר הבית.
steps.whatToRemember: The impure כהן could not stay in the עזרה or on the הר הבית. He could use the tunnels only because, according to רבי יוחנן, they were never made holy.

steps.title: רב ספרא invites רבי אבא into the בית הכסא
steps.stepSummary: On the משנה's line about the lamps and the בית הכסא, the גמרא tells a story. רב ספרא was in the בית הכסא, רבי אבא coughed outside, and רב ספרא told him to come in.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said: and the lamps were burning on this side and that side, etc. רב ספרא was sitting in the בית הכסא. רבי אבא came and coughed to him. רב ספרא said to him: Come in, Master!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tells a story that sets up a lesson from the משנה about privacy in the בית הכסא. The lesson comes in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There was no door, so רבי אבא coughed to find out if someone was inside. Instead of letting him wait, רב ספרא invited him in while he was still there.

keyTerms.meaning: Coughed or cleared his throat, as a signal

phrases.english: And the lamps were burning on this side and on that side, etc.

phrases.aramaic: רַב סָפְרָא הֲוָה יָתֵיב בְּבֵית הַכִּסֵּא,
phrases.english: Rav Safra was sitting in the bathroom,
Rabbi Abba came and coughed to him.
He said to him: Let the Master enter!

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב סָפְרָא הֲוָה יָתֵיב בְּבֵית הַכִּסֵּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves on to the next line of the משנה and opens a new topic with a story.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A story: רב ספרא invited רבי אבא into the בית הכסא while he himself was inside.

steps.title: רבי אבא rebukes רב ספרא using the משנה
steps.stepSummary: רבי אבא tells רב ספרא he acted like the people of שעיר. He proves from the משנה that a person should not go in while someone else is inside.
steps.simpleTranslation: After he came out, רבי אבא said to him: You never went up to שעיר, yet you learned the ways of שעיר?! Didn't we learn this in the משנה: If he found it closed, it was known that a person was there! That shows he should not go in!
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אבא challenges רב ספרא's behavior and uses the משנה to prove it was wrong.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה says a closed door meant someone was inside, so the next person would wait outside. That shows the proper way is not to go in while someone is there. So רב ספרא should not have invited רבי אבא in. Calling it the ways of שעיר is a sharp way of saying this was immodest behavior.

keyTerms.meaning: The land of אדום, here a picture of immodest behavior
This comes to say, meaning this shows that

steps.whatToRemember: From the משנה's honorable בית הכסא we learn about modesty: normally you do not go in while someone else is inside. The next step explains why רב ספרא still invited רבי אבא in.
steps.confusionAlert: רבי אבא is not saying רב ספרא actually traveled to שעיר. He is saying that even without going there, רב ספרא picked up their immodest habits.

phrases.aramaic: בָּתַר דְּנָפֵיק, אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַבִּי אַבָּא:
phrases.english: After he came out, Rabbi Abba said to him:
Until now you have not gone up to Seir,
yet you have learned the ways of Seir?!
Didn't we learn this in the mishna:

phrases.aramaic: מְצָאוֹ נָעוּל – בְּיָדוּעַ שֶׁיֵּשׁ שָׁם אָדָם!
phrases.english: If he found it closed, it was known that there was a person there!
This is to say that he should not enter!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: רבי אבא challenges רב ספרא's invitation from step 16 using the משנה. The next step defends רב ספרא.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב ספרא's invitation to רבי אבא to enter the בית הכסא while he was inside.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The משנה shows that a closed door signaled someone was inside and others would wait. So entering while someone is inside is improper.
steps.whyThisMatters: It turns a detail of the מקדש's layout into a lasting rule of modesty for everyone.

steps.title: רב ספרא worried that holding it in was dangerous
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא defends רב ספרא. He told רבי אבא to come in because he feared that waiting could harm רבי אבא's health. A ברייתא of רבן שמעון בן גמליאל teaches that holding it in causes illness.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב ספרא thought: maybe he is in danger. As a ברייתא teaches, רבן שמעון בן גמליאל says: holding back stool causes swelling sickness, and holding back urine causes jaundice.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers רבי אבא's complaint from Step 17. רב ספרא had a good reason for inviting him in: he was worried about רבי אבא's health.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי אבא said one should not go in while someone else is inside. The answer is that health comes first. If רבי אבא held it in while waiting outside, he could get sick, as the ברייתא warns.

keyTerms.meaning: Holding back stool. Literally, a column that is pushed back.
A sickness where the body swells with fluid
Holding back urine. Literally, a stream that is pushed back.
Jaundice, a sickness that turns the skin yellow

steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that protecting a person's health can override a rule of proper conduct.

phrases.english: And Rav Safra thought:
Perhaps he is in danger.
phrases.notes: He means רבי אבא, who was waiting outside and might be hurt by holding it in.

phrases.aramaic: כִּדְתַנְיָא, רַבָּן שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן גַּמְלִיאֵל אוֹמֵר:
phrases.english: As it was taught: Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel says:
A column of stool that is held back
brings a person to swelling sickness,
a stream of urine that is held back
brings a person to jaundice.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרַב סָפְרָא סָבַר: דִּלְמָא מְסוּכָּן הוּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רבי אבא's challenge by explaining רב ספרא's reason.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Gives the reason behind the action: concern for health outweighs the rule of conduct.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רב ספרא acted improperly, like the people of שעיר.
steps.terutzMaskana: רב ספרא acted out of concern that רבי אבא might be in danger from holding it in.

steps.title: Fathers' advice on timing and modesty in the bathroom
steps.stepSummary: רב told his son חייא, and רב הונא told his son רבה: relieve yourself at nightfall and before dawn so you won't need to go far away. Sit before you uncover yourself, and cover yourself before you stand up.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב said to his son חייא, and רב הונא said to his son רבה: When it gets dark, take care of yourself, and early in the morning, take care of yourself, so that you won't have to go far. Sit and then uncover. Cover and then stand.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא continues the topic of health and the bathroom with practical advice two great אמוראים gave their sons.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Going at times when the streets are empty means you never have to hold it in while searching for a private place, which fits the health worry from Step 18. The second piece of advice is about modesty: stay covered for as long as possible.

keyTerms.meaning: Take care of yourself. A polite way of saying relieve yourself.

phrases.english: Rav said to his son Ḥiyya,

phrases.aramaic: וְכֵן אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַב הוּנָא לְרַבָּה בְּרֵיהּ:
phrases.english: and likewise Rav Huna said to his son Rabba:
When it gets dark, relieve yourself,
and early, before daybreak, relieve yourself,
so that you will not have to go far away.
Sit, and then uncover yourself.
Cover yourself, and then stand up.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַב לְחִיָּיא בְּרֵיהּ, וְכֵן אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַב הוּנָא לְרַבָּה בְּרֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Builds on the health concern from Step 18 with practical advice.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Go at night and before dawn so you won't need to hold it in. Sit before uncovering, and cover before standing.

steps.title: Rinse the cup and pour out water before passing it on
steps.stepSummary: The same fathers' advice continues: rinse the cup before drinking and before putting it down. When drinking water, pour some out before giving the cup to your student.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rinse and drink. Rinse and put it down. And when you drink water, pour some of it out, and afterward give it to your student.
steps.whatsHappening: The advice of רב and רב הונא to their sons continues, now about drinking from a cup.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Rinsing keeps the cup clean for whoever uses it next. Pouring out some water from a cup you drank from washes the rim, so your student won't feel disgusted to drink after you.

phrases.english: Rinse the cup, and then drink.
Rinse it, and then put it down.
phrases.notes: The word in square brackets is added in the corrected wording; some versions don't have it.

phrases.english: And when you drink water,
pour out some of it,
and afterward give it to your student.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the same list of advice from Step 19.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Rinse the cup before and after drinking. When you drink water, pour some out before handing the cup to your student.

steps.title: A student who died of thirst
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא supports the rule about pouring out water. A teacher once gave his student a cup without pouring some out. The student was very sensitive, refused to drink, and died of thirst. After that, the חכמים made the rule.
steps.simpleTranslation: As a ברייתא teaches: A person should not drink water and give it to his student unless he poured some out. There was a story about someone who drank water, did not pour any out, and gave it to his student. That student was very sensitive, did not want to drink, and died of thirst. At that time they said: A person should not drink water and give it to his student unless he poured some out.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא to show where the advice in Step 20 comes from. A tragic story explains why the rule was made.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The student was so sensitive that he could not bring himself to drink from the cup his teacher had drunk from, and he died of thirst. Pouring some water out first rinses the rim, so even a sensitive student can drink. That is why the חכמים made this a rule.

keyTerms.meaning: A very sensitive or delicate person who is easily disgusted

steps.confusionAlert: The rule is aimed at the teacher, not the student. The teacher must pour out water before handing over his cup.

phrases.english: As it was taught:

phrases.aramaic: לֹא יִשְׁתֶּה אָדָם מַיִם וְיִתֵּן לְתַלְמִידוֹ,
phrases.english: A person should not drink water and give it to his student,
unless he poured some of it out.
And there was a story about someone who drank water
and did not pour any of it out, and gave it to his student,
and that student was a very sensitive person,
and he did not want to drink, and he died of thirst.
At that time they said:

phrases.aramaic: לֹא יִשְׁתֶּה אָדָם מַיִם וְיִתֵּן לְתַלְמִידוֹ
phrases.english: A person should not drink water and give it to his student
unless he poured some of it out.

steps.triggerLanguage: כִּדְתַנְיָא: לֹא יִשְׁתֶּה אָדָם מַיִם וְיִתֵּן לְתַלְמִידוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the source and the story behind the advice in Step 20.
steps.raayaObject: The advice to pour out water before giving the cup to a student
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא with the story of the sensitive student who died of thirst

steps.title: A student may pour out water in front of his teacher
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי concludes from the ברייתא that a student who pours out some water in front of his teacher is not being disrespectful.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אשי said: Therefore, a student who pours out water in front of his teacher is not doing anything disrespectful.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי draws a practical conclusion from the story about the student who died of thirst.
steps.deeperAnalysis: One might think that pouring out water from the teacher's cup in front of him looks like a hint that the teacher's cup is dirty, which would be an insult. Since the חכמים required pouring out water for this very reason, doing it is normal and proper, not rude.
steps.whatToRemember: Health and dignity come first: you don't hold it in, and you don't make a sensitive person drink from a dirty cup. A student who pours out water from his teacher's cup is not being disrespectful.

phrases.english: Rav Ashi said: Therefore,
this student who pours out water in front of his teacher
is not doing anything disrespectful.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws a practical conclusion from the ברייתא in Step 21.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: Since the חכמים required pouring out water, a student who does it in front of his teacher is not being disrespectful.

steps.title: Do not spit in front of your teacher, except after gourd or porridge
steps.stepSummary: The fathers' advice ends: never spit in front of your רבי, except after eating gourd or porridge, because that saliva is like molten lead.
steps.simpleTranslation: Whatever you eat, do not spit it out in front of your teacher, except gourd and porridge, because they are like a bar of lead.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the last piece of advice from רב and רב הונא to their sons. Spitting in front of your teacher is disrespectful, but there is one exception.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Spitting in front of a רבי is normally disrespectful. Gourd and porridge are an exception because their saliva is heavy and harmful, 'like lead.' This matches the earlier steps: when health is at risk, the usual rules of respect give way.

keyTerms.meaning: in front of, in the presence of
a bar (or wick) of lead, an image for something heavy and harmful

steps.whatToRemember: All the fathers' advice follows one idea: respect your teacher, but never at the cost of your health. That is why רבי אבא was told to come in, why the student may pour out water, and why one may spit after gourd or porridge.

phrases.english: Anything, do not spit it out
phrases.notes: He means saliva that builds up while you are eating.

phrases.english: in front of your teacher,
except for gourd and porridge,
because they are like a bar of lead.
phrases.notes: Holding in this saliva is as harmful as swallowing hot lead, so you may spit it out.

steps.triggerLanguage: כׇּל מִילֵּי לָא תִּיפְלוֹט בְּאַפֵּי רַבָּךְ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues and closes the list of advice the fathers gave their sons, after the water-pouring rule and the proof for it.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Do not spit in front of your teacher, except after gourd or porridge, where holding it in is dangerous.

steps.title: Quoting the משנה about the איש הר הבית checking the guards
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא opens a new section by quoting a משנה: the איש הר הבית went around every guard post with torches. It then speaks of a post where the guard did not stand up and greet him, saying 'איש הר הבית...'. The quote continues on the next amud.
steps.simpleTranslation: We learned there in a משנה: the איש הר הבית would go around to each and every guard post, with burning torches in front of him. And any guard post where the guard did not stand up and say to him: 'איש הר הבית...'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא changes topic and quotes a משנה from מסכת מדות as a base text. This is a setup. The quote continues on the next amud, and the גמרא will then discuss it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The איש הר הבית checked that the guards were awake. The torches let the guards see him coming, so an awake guard would stand up. An awake guard would stand and greet him with 'איש הר הבית...'. A guard who did not do so showed that he was asleep. The rest of this rule comes on the next amud.

keyTerms.meaning: the man of the Temple Mount, the officer in charge of the night guards
a guard post, or the guards on watch there

steps.confusionAlert: Here the guard is the one who should speak. שאינו עומד ואומר לו means a guard who does not stand up and say to the officer. The words 'איש הר הבית' at the end begin the guard's greeting to the officer, which continues on the next amud.

phrases.english: We learned there:
phrases.notes: "There" means a משנה in a different מסכת, מדות 1:2.

phrases.english: The man of the Temple Mount

phrases.aramaic: הָיָה מְחַזֵּר עַל כָּל מִשְׁמָר וּמִשְׁמָר,
phrases.english: would go around to each and every guard post,
with burning torches in front of him.
And any guard post where the guard does not stand up
and say to him: "Man of the Temple Mount...

steps.triggerLanguage: תְּנַן הָתָם: אִישׁ הַר הַבַּיִת הָיָה מְחַזֵּר עַל כָּל מִשְׁמָר וּמִשְׁמָר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new topic. The advice to the sons is finished, and the גמרא now brings a משנה from מסכת מדות about the Temple guards.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The איש הר הבית made rounds with torches, and the guard who did not stand up and say to him 'איש הר הבית...' is the subject of the next clause (the quote continues).
